## Verdict

wrong

## Bearer

RaceRecordingRepositoryImpl — app-wear/src/main/java/com/mgilli/app_wear/race/RaceRecordingRepositoryImpl.kt, publishRecorded

## Trigger

publishRecorded, called after every race state mutation (startClock, markSegment and the other writers) — observed

## Today

ImportPreviewViewModel.onSaveClicked (app-phone) dates an imported race
at `raceDate.atStartOfDay(ZoneId.systemDefault()).toInstant()`, so a
second race imported on the same calendar day carries the same
`date` instant as the first.

On the phone, RaceDao's query orders `SELECT * FROM races ORDER BY
dateEpochMs DESC, id DESC` — an explicit second key breaks the tie,
and `ImportPreviewViewModelTest` / the DAO's own tests exercise it.

On the watch, RaceRecordingRepositoryImpl.publishRecorded orders the
in-memory races with `races.values.filter { ... }.reversed()
.sortedByDescending { it.date }`. The comment above it says the
intent is the same tie-break as the phone (id, descending, via
insertion order): `reversed()` puts the most recently inserted race
first, and `sortedByDescending` is relied on to be a *stable* sort so
that reversed order survives as the tie-break for races sharing a
`date`. Nothing in the code compares `id` (or any second key)
explicitly — the ordering depends entirely on `sortedByDescending`
staying a stable sort. If that call were ever replaced by an
unstable sort, or by anything else that does not preserve input
order among equal keys, races imported on the same day would reorder
silently, with no test able to catch it since the current behaviour
is correct by accident of implementation, not by an assertion the
code makes.

## Expected

publishRecorded orders races by an explicit second key, `id`
descending, the same two keys the phone's query uses — e.g.
`races.values.filter { ... }.sortedWith(compareByDescending<Race> {
it.date }.thenByDescending { it.id })` — so the ordering no longer
depends on `sortedByDescending`'s stability or on `reversed()`
priming the tie-break through insertion order.
